meta.title: GLP-1 Agonists Are Associated With a Significant Reduction in Breast Cancer Incidence in Women.
meta.abstract:
Purpose

Excess weight is a key modifiable risk factor for breast cancer. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1) promote weight loss and improve metabolic health, but their effect on breast cancer risk remains unclear.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study from January 1, 2022, to June 30, 2025, using electronic health records. We identified 217,624 unique women who underwent breast imaging; restricting to ages 45-80 years with a BMI ≥25 and a documented imaging outcome (n = 111,646; median age 61 years). The primary outcome was breast cancer detection. GLP-1 use was defined as a first prescription before the examination date and assessed in relation to race, ethnicity, age, and type 2 diabetes. To address potential confounding between these covariates and GLP-1 exposure, we performed one-to-one, case-control matching using propensity scores on the basis of age, race, ethnicity, highest BMI, breast density, and history of type 2 diabetes. The propensity matching to the GLP-1 use group was performed using the greedy nearest neighbor approach.

Results

GLP-1 exposure was associated with a lower incidence of breast cancer (odds ratio [OR], 0.649 [95% CI, 0.569 to 0.741]; P < .0001). In the matched logistic regression (30,528 observations; 600 cancer cases), GLP-1 exposure was associated with a lower breast cancer incidence (OR, 0.695 [95% CI, 0.590 to 0.819]; P < .0001).

Conclusion

In this large observational study of women undergoing breast imaging at a major academic center and affiliated sites, GLP-1 treatment was associated with a lower incidence of breast cancer, independent of age, race, ethnicity, BMI, breast density, and diabetes. The findings support the need for prospective trials investigating GLP-1 agonists for breast cancer prevention.

domains.name: Measurement of the exposure
domains.direction_justification: Exposure was defined as any single prescription documented before the examination date across a short study window (January 1, 2022 to June 30, 2025). Classifying patients with minimal or acute pre-index exposure as protected against solid tumor oncogenesis—which requires a multi-year latency period—produces severe reverse causality and immortal time bias away from the null.

findings.title: Absence of cumulative dose, duration, or latency requirements
findings.mechanism: Solid tumors such as breast cancer require years to develop clinically. Defining exposure as at least one prescription without minimum treatment duration or a latency window allows incident cancers already present preclinical to be categorized as non-exposed if diagnosed shortly before or around prescription initiation, creating an artificial protective association.
evidence: Study timeframe is 3.5 years (January 1, 2022 to June 30, 2025)
Exposure defined as 'first prescription before the examination date' with no requirement for minimum duration of therapy or cumulative dose

findings.title: Unverified adherence and out-of-system exposure misclassification
findings.mechanism: Prescription orders in EHRs do not confirm dispensing or adherence, and patients obtaining GLP-1 agonists through third-party telehealth or compounding pharmacies are misclassified as unexposed controls.
evidence: Authors acknowledge: 'there could be patients on GLP-1 agonists who obtained these drugs outside of our health system, including non-FDA-approved doses and formulations at compounding pharmacies'

findings.title: Absence of lag period and follow-up shorter than tumor latency
findings.mechanism: Solid tumors like breast cancer take years to develop clinically. Without a lag period, immediate post-prescription non-events or events reflect preexisting disease processes rather than true preventive drug effects.
evidence: The primary outcome was a malignant breast pathology diagnosis during the study period.
We also did not require a minimum duration of therapy, because exposure is not definitely related to dose

findings.title: Prevalent user and immortal time bias from ever-use definition prior to exam
findings.mechanism: Defining exposure as any first prescription prior to an index examination date without establishing an incident new-user cohort with lookback washout introduces immortal time and survivor bias in the exposed group.
evidence: GLP-1 agonist use was defined as a first prescription before the examination date
reduction in breast cancer diagnoses within the study group associated with any prior or current use of GLP-1 agonist.

domains.name: Selection of participants into the study
domains.direction_justification: Restricting the cohort to patients undergoing breast imaging creates collider stratification bias: GLP-1 users undergo more frequent clinical encounters and routine screening mammography, while non-users undergoing imaging may have a higher proportion of diagnostic evaluations for symptomatic breast lumps, artificially inflating the cancer rate in non-users (2.47% unmatched, 2.31% matched vs 1.62% in GLP-1 users).

findings.title: Collider conditioning on breast imaging participation
findings.mechanism: Selecting solely patients with documented breast imaging conditions on healthcare engagement and imaging indications. If unexposed individuals in the imaging database are enriched for diagnostic imaging of symptomatic lumps while GLP-1 users are undergoing routine surveillance, the observed cancer risk among unexposed controls is biased upward.
evidence: Cohort restricted to 111,646 women aged 45-80 with BMI >= 25 who underwent breast imaging between 2022 and 2025

domains.name: Post-exposure interventions
domains.direction_justification: Differential downstream clinical management, lifestyle interventions, and co-prescriptions (such as SGLT2 inhibitors or statins) between GLP-1 users and controls were not tracked or adjusted during the study period.

findings.title: Unmeasured concomitant treatments and weight loss interventions
findings.mechanism: Co-interventions initiated after GLP-1 prescription (e.g., intensive nutritional counseling, changes in metabolic pharmacotherapy) could independently alter cancer risk biomarkers or screening behaviors.
evidence: No data provided on post-index lifestyle interventions or changes in concurrent medications

domains.name: Missing data
domains.direction_justification: A substantial proportion of the initial imaging population (54,799 of 166,445 women aged 45-80, or 32.9%) was excluded due to BMI < 25 or missing BMI / lack of documented imaging outcome, with no sensitivity analysis or multiple imputation performed.

findings.title: Exclusion of patients without complete EHR BMI or imaging outcomes
findings.mechanism: Complete case exclusion of 54,799 patients without examining missingness mechanisms could introduce bias if missingness in BMI or outcome documentation was related to clinical prognosis or drug prescription.
evidence: 166,445 women aged 45-80 reduced to 111,646 (32.9% excluded for BMI < 25 or missing outcome/data)

domains.name: Measurement of the outcome
domains.direction_justification: Outcome capture was restricted to malignant breast pathology documented within a single health system EHR; any out-of-system cancer diagnoses would be non-differentially missed, attenuating effect estimates toward the null.

findings.title: Health-system EHR-restricted cancer diagnosis ascertainment
findings.mechanism: Malignant diagnoses made at external institutions or regional cancer centers without reciprocal EHR records are missed, potentially leading to outcome underascertainment.
evidence: Outcome defined solely as malignant breast pathology diagnosis documented in the health system EHR during the 2022-2025 study period

domains.name: Selection of the reported result
domains.direction_justification: As a retrospective EHR analysis lacking a publicly registered prospective protocol, reported models and matching specifications could be subject to selective model selection favoring statistically significant inverse associations.

findings.title: Retrospective design without pre-registered statistical analysis plan
findings.mechanism: Post-hoc decisions regarding matching caliper, covarariate definitions (e.g. maximum BMI from 2017-2025), and model parameters can increase the probability of selecting favorable effect sizes.
evidence: Single-institution retrospective EHR database study with no trial registry or prospective SAP cited

overall.summary: The study exhibits a very high overall risk of bias driven by critical flaws in exposure definition, biological implausibility of the time-to-event window, and confounding. Exposure was defined as any single prescription before an imaging exam within a short 3.5-year observation window (2022-2025), ignoring biological tumor latency and introducing severe immortal time bias and reverse causality. Furthermore, propensity matching failed to balance prior breast cancer history (7.8% in unexposed vs 5.9% in GLP-1 exposed, Table A2) and omitted core breast cancer risk factors (family history, reproductive factors, exogenous hormones), while conditioning the entire cohort on undergoing breast imaging generated selection/collider bias. Consequently, the observed 30.5% odds reduction (matched OR 0.695) is predominantly an artifact of methodological confounding and selection rather than a causal preventive effect.
